lessons.title: AI and everyday tools
lessons.subtitle: Week 1: Recognising AI
lessons.body:
AI systems perform tasks such as recognising speech, predicting outcomes, and generating content. A simple calculator can follow fixed rules without learning from examples.

Offline practice: Compare a calculator, a voice assistant, and a paper timetable; identify where patterns or fixed rules are used. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.
takeaways: AI systems perform tasks such as recognising speech, predicting outcomes, and generating content. A simple calculator can follow fixed rules without learning from examples.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
lessons.sourceName: Google Machine Learning Crash Course — further reading

lessons.title: Prediction and generation
lessons.subtitle: Week 1: Recognising AI
lessons.body:
A prediction model estimates an outcome from input. A generative model produces content. A system that estimates tomorrow’s demand differs from one that drafts an announcement.

Offline practice: Write one prediction task and one content-generation task for a fictional community library. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

lessons.title: What a model represents
lessons.subtitle: Week 1: Recognising AI
lessons.body:
A model is a mathematical representation used to transform inputs into outputs. It is a simplified system, not a complete description of the world.

Offline practice: Sketch input → model → output for a fictional tool that classifies messages as spam. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

lessons.title: Human judgement
lessons.subtitle: Week 1: Recognising AI
lessons.body:

lessons.title: Your first AI map
lessons.subtitle: Week 1: Recognising AI
lessons.body:
A useful AI map names the task, input, output, benefit, limitation, and human reviewer. Some tasks are better handled with a checklist or ordinary software.

Offline practice: Create an AI map for organising revision notes and explain when a paper checklist would be enough. Write your reasoning before looking at the quiz answers. Record one limitation or uncertainty. You can use paper or local notes; an online AI tool is optional.

Recap: explain yesterday’s key idea from memory, then check your notes. After a break, start with this recap and the first small step of today’s activity.

Complete all three quiz questions before moving on.

Weekly completion task: save this week’s practice artifact. Confirm four steps: explain a key idea (recap); complete the practice activity (practice); record what you would verify and where (plan); show your artifact and explain one improvement (demonstrate).
takeaways: A useful AI map names the task, input, output, benefit, limitation, and human reviewer. Some tasks are better handled with a checklist or ordinary software.
Apply the idea through the offline activity.
Keep reasoning, evidence, and limitations with your artifact.
